content:
Priya: Quick heads-up — final SRE candidate (Ravi K) panels TOMORROW 11:30am PT. Need a scribe + 2 code reviewers. Panel so far: Samir, Elena, Jordan.
Samir: I can do interview + system-design. Which PRs/docs should I skim?
Priya: Thanks — main PRs are: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/492 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/118. Focus on runbook clarity, test coverage, and rollback plan.
Elena: I'll take a look at both PRs. @Jordan can you be scribe? Also we need Zoom + recording permissions confirmed.
Jordan: Yep I can scribe. Zoom link created and recording enabled. Will paste link in calendar.
DevEx: Quick ops ask — can we get a 2–3 line interview prompt for an oncall triage scenario to use during systems judgement?
Priya: Sure — sample prompt to use:
```
Candidate paged at 02:00 for sudden tokenization latency spike. You have 20 minutes to triage — what do you check first, immediate mitigations, and rollback thresholds? Keep answers actionable.
```
Samir: Perfect. For scoring: use 1–5 per category. Weighting i'll use: technical 40%, systems judgement 30%, collaboration 20%, culture-fit 10%.
Elena: Small rubric clarification: does "systems judgement" include cost/latency tradeoffs and rollback economics?
Priya: Yes — include cost tradeoffs, SLA impacts, and clear rollback criteria.
Jordan: Scribe note: we'll use the shared GDrive debrief doc (link posted in calendar). I will capture timestamps and key decisions.
People Ops Bot: Reminder scheduled — 15 minutes before the panel. Post-interview debrief form: https://forms.redwood/candidate-debrief
Samir: :thumbsup: I'll skim PR #492 tonight and note any open questions.
Elena: Thanks — i'll flag any flaky tests or missing metrics.
Priya: Reminder for panelists: please submit scores within 24h after interview. :memo: If you can't, ping here and we'll extend window.
Jordan: If anyone needs pre-read summaries, shoot them to me and i'll drop TL;DR in the doc.
DevEx: One last note — can reviewers call out specific lines in PRs for scoring (e.g., test cases / observability hooks)? that helps calibration.
Priya: Absolutely — callouts are helpful. See you all tomorrow.
